title: Cold rebuild: the offset tracker
summary: Rebuild OffsetTracker from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You wrote **Track the safe commit position** in *Per-key order at scale*. Now write it
again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you
Why this one? Every consumer that processes in parallel needs it, and getting it wrong loses data silently: commit one
offset too far and a crash skips records nobody ever handled.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Offsets 40 to 44 were handed to workers. 41, 42 and 44 are done; 40 and 43 are still running. Which offset is safe to commit?
explain: A committed offset means "everything below this is done". 40 is still running, so nothing beyond 40 can be committed:
after a crash the group restarts at 40 and redoes 41, 42 and 44 (at-least-once, so the handler must be idempotent).

steps.title: Rebuild the offset tracker cold
prompt: Write the class `OffsetTracker` again, from memory.
- `void Started(long offset)`: the record was handed to a worker.
- `void Done(long offset)`: a worker finished it (any order).
- `long? Committable`: `null` while nothing has finished; otherwise the smallest offset still in flight, or the
highest finished offset + 1 when nothing is in flight.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
